item.title: Poetry the Heart of things
item.description: Yesterday a small group of us met in the church library. The intent of the group is to meet on a regular basis and to read poetry together after the model of lectio divina. This is a practice that is very old and aims to listen to a text, closely and over several repetitions, paying attention to a circle of voices ranging from the words in front of us, the godly voice of the universe, and the voice of our conscience sending us into action or metanoia.

item.title: Embarrasement
item.description: Embarasement and Shame Quiet day of prayer. 9 o’clock in the morning the Miata didn’t turn over but then on about the third try there was a pop. One more try and it started. Temperature was 75 but presumably it had been rising all morning long so the temperature is clearly a factor. The point of the blogs for me was to find my voice. To counteract my sense of marching to somebody else’s drums.

item.title: Poem
item.description: Poem for today A day that allowed for roaming and circling While the prayer group took aim at a labyrinth. Thin places, they speak to me, My significant space, what previously I might have called Spirit, opens up like a lily bud turning toward its prime mover. They said of him at the time for eulogies That he had formed the habit of leaving a space, a room, a clean-up effort, or the tidying of the evening colloquy,

item.title: Episcopal Church circa 2016
item.description: The Episcopal Church circa 2016 TOC {:toc} The setting: a call to double the size of a shrinking Episcopal Church I am grateful and inspired by The Rev. Tom Buechele’s recent email, shared with the retired clergy of the diocese of Hawai’i. In it he took note of the seemingly extreme demand for supply clergy in remote congregations. He had received requests from as far away as Mexico. He wondered about the health of the church where so many Episcopalians were not able to get the sacraments on a Sunday morning.
